ru.title: Умное обучение с учетом переносимости
ru.desc: Статья описывает методику Transfer-Aware Curriculum (TAC), которая улучшает обучение с подкреплением в нескольких доменах. TAC определяет приоритетные домены для обучения, которые способствуют улучшению результатов в других доменах, используя выравнивание градиентов для оценки переносимости. Это позволяет адаптировать учебный план в реальном времени и повышает точность на различных задачах, таких как математика и программирование. Тесты показывают, что TAC значительно превосходит традиционные методы и сохраняет эффективность даже в условиях неравномерного обучения.

en.title: Boosting Multi-Domain Learning with Transfer-Aware Curriculum
en.desc: The paper introduces Transfer-Aware Curriculum (TAC), a method that enhances multi-domain reinforcement learning by focusing on domains that can help improve others. It uses gradient-geometry alignment to assess how updates in one domain can benefit the learning in other domains. Unlike traditional methods that rely on fixed sampling or hand-tuning, TAC adapts dynamically to prioritize domains that maximize overall learning efficiency. The results show that TAC significantly outperforms existing curriculum strategies, demonstrating the importance of cross-domain transferability in designing effective training schedules.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Quantum-Inspired Fast Weight Programmers for Traffic-Matrix Forecasting
papers.abstract: Abstract Quantum-inspired recurrent models using gated QKAN-FWPs demonstrate superior forecasting accuracy with reduced computational requirements compared to traditional LSTM networks for traffic matrix prediction.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Traffic matrices (TMs) capture network-wide origin-destination demand and are central to traffic engineering, yet accurate whole-matrix forecasting remains challenging when prediction must be performed under the memory, update, and training-budget constraints of online network control. This paper investigates whether compact quantum-inspired recurrent models can provide effective TM forecasts without relying on dedicated graph, transformer, or diffusion modules. We adapt gated quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold network fast-weight programmers (QKAN-FWPs) to direct multi-step Abilene TM forecasting, where each model predicts the next 20 five-minute frames of a 144-channel origin-destination (OD) matrix from a two-hour history. We benchmark three QKAN placement variants against a matched-size long short-term memory (LSTM) network, a larger LSTM, and a classical gated fast-weight programmer under a shared fixed-budget training protocol. Among the evaluated recurrent models, G-QKANFWP achieves the best pooled root-mean-square error (RMSE), while using only 22.4% of the larger LSTM. It also outperforms both the matched-size LSTM and the classical G-FWP baseline, indicating that the gain is not due to gated fast-weight framework alone. Convergence and channel-wise analyses further show that the quantum-inspired variants obtain lower validation-loss area under the learning curve (AULC) than matched-size recurrent baselines, while G-QKANFWP and GQKAN-FWP achieve substantially more OD-channel wins. These results identify a classical slow programmer with a quantum-inspired fast programmer as a promising accuracy-efficiency design for resource-conscious network traffic-matrix forecasting.

ru.title: Квантовые модели для точного прогнозирования трафика
ru.desc: В статье рассматриваются квантово-вдохновленные рекуррентные модели, которые показывают повышенную точность прогнозирования матриц трафика по сравнению с традиционными LSTM-сетями. Модели используют адаптированные квантовые программы для быстрого обновления весов, что позволяет эффективно предсказывать матрицы с высоким разрешением. Эксперименты продемонстрировали, что новая модель G-QKAN-FWP достигает лучших результатов при меньших вычислительных затратах. Это открывает новые горизонты для проектирования систем прогнозирования с ограниченными ресурсами.

en.title: Quantum-Inspired Models Revolutionize Traffic Forecasting
en.desc: This paper presents quantum-inspired recurrent models, specifically gated QKAN-FWPs, which enhance forecasting accuracy for traffic matrices while being more computationally efficient than traditional LSTM networks. Traffic matrices are crucial for understanding network demand, but predicting them accurately is difficult under constraints of online network control. The study adapts QKAN-FWPs to forecast multi-step traffic matrices, demonstrating that these models can predict future traffic demands effectively. Results show that G-QKAN-FWP outperforms LSTM models in accuracy and efficiency, suggesting a new approach for resource-conscious traffic forecasting.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Grid-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in High Dimensions
papers.abstract: Abstract Grid-based multiprobe algorithms demonstrate superior dimensional scaling properties compared to graph-, tree-, and partitioning-based methods for approximate nearest neighbor search, making them competitive for high-dimensional and rebuild-heavy applications.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Grid-based approaches to approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search have been absent from modern scaling analyses. We present a systematic characterization of a multiprobe grid algorithm with respect to dataset size N and dimensionality d. Our experiments reveal a previously unreported d-scaling crossover on the GloVe embedding family, in which multiprobe grid search maintains an approximately constant dimensional scaling exponent while other graph-, tree-, and partitioning-based methods exhibit degrading throughput. The advantage comes with near-linear query scaling in N, but also with lower indexing cost than competing ANN methods. Our results suggest that grid-based methods such as multiprobe grid may be competitive in rebuild-heavy or high-dimensional settings where indexing cost and dimensional robustness dictate performance. More broadly, recent work has formalized self-attention as an ANN operation. Thus, the N- and d-scaling properties of ANN algorithms may guide cost analysis of efficient transformer architectures. Code is available at: https://github.com/weiz345/MultiProbeANN.

ru.title: Превосходство сетевых алгоритмов в поясе поиска соседей
ru.desc: В данной статье рассматриваются алгоритмы поиска ближайших соседей на основе сетки, которые показывают лучшие свойства масштабируемости по сравнению с графовыми, древовидными и партиционными методами. Мы систематически охарактеризовали алгоритм мультипроба с точки зрения размера набора данных N и размерности d. Эксперименты показали, что мультипроба поддерживает почти постоянный масштабирование размерности при росте N, в то время как другие методы демонстрируют ухудшение производительности. Результаты указывают на преимущества использования методов на основе сетки в задаче поиска ближайших соседей при высоких размерностях и значительных затратах на перестройку индекса.

en.title: Grid-Based Methods: A New Frontier in ANN Search
en.desc: This paper explores grid-based multiprobe algorithms for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search, highlighting their advantages in high-dimensional and rebuild-heavy applications. The authors systematically analyze the performance of a multiprobe grid algorithm in relation to dataset size and dimensionality. They discover a unique scaling behavior where the multiprobe grid method maintains efficiency while other methods struggle as dimensions increase. The findings suggest that grid-based approaches could be more effective in scenarios where indexing costs and dimensionality are critical factors.
